title: APAC Quarterly: Navigating Australia’s mixed macro landscape
gist: World Gold Council argues Australia faces stagflationary pressure (trimmed-mean CPI 3.6%, GDP 2.1%, RBA at 4.6%), with bond-equity correlations at multi-decade highs making gold a better diversifier.

insights.claim: Australia's trimmed-mean CPI accelerated four quarters in a row to 3.6% y/y in Q2 2026, driven by expiry of electricity rebates and Middle East-linked fuel prices.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Inflation pressure limits RBA's room to ease.

insights.claim: Australian GDP slowed for a second quarter to 2.1% y/y in Q2 and unemployment rose to 4.6% in August, the highest since November 2021.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Growth is softening while inflation accelerates.

insights.claim: The RBA has hiked four times in 2026, taking the policy rate to 4.6%, the highest in almost 15 years, and home sales have felt the pressure.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil

insights.claim: Australian bonds and equities are more correlated than ever, undermining bonds as a diversifier, while gold's correlation with Australian equities has stayed negative.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold is a better hedge than bonds in a 60/40 portfolio.
insights.locator: Gold should remain a strategic asset

insights.claim: Gold's correlation with equities falls in stock pullbacks and rises when stocks climb, cushioning losses while retaining gains.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold behaves convexly relative to equities.
insights.locator: Gold should remain a strategic asset

insights.claim: Gold in AUD has oscillated between A$6,000 and A$6,500 per ounce, and past Fed hiking cycles show no uniform gold response because short-term yields and fiscal fears in long-term yields pull in opposite directions.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Don't assume Fed hikes are uniformly negative for gold.
insights.locator: Gold should remain a strategic asset

insights.claim: Australian jewellery demand was 1t in Q2 (-4% y/y) and bar and coin demand plunged 59% y/y to 1.5t, but gold ETF holdings reached a record 55t after 2.6t of H2 buying.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Physical retail demand is weak while ETF demand is rebuilding.
